title: Per-domain exemplar anchoring and adaptive oversampling for calibration packs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a repeatable workflow to produce per-domain calibration packs used for FP8 and INT8 quantization that balances fidelity to production prompt distributions with robustness for low-volume domains. The goal is to generate compact, high-signal calibration datasets (per-domain packs) that drive stable quantization profiles and minimize accuracy regressions in downstream metrics.
background: Our quantization pipeline currently uses global calibration sets and simple stratified sampling. For diverse product domains (search, summarization, code-assist, finance), global packs underrepresent domain-specific tokens and prompting patterns, causing localized accuracy regressions after INT8/FP8 quantization. Past attempts (decay-weighting, domain-aware replay) improved some domains but created calibration drift for long-tail domains. We need a packaging strategy that anchors exemplar prompts per domain, adaptively oversamples low-volume but high-severity domains, and provides clear validation steps.
proposal: 1) Build a per-domain exemplar index: for each domain, select 200-800 exemplars via a hybrid score combining recent traffic weight, semantic diversity (embedding clustering), and error-proneness (historical inference/regression deltas). 2) Anchor set: always include top 25 exemplars per domain as immutable anchors for regression detection. 3) Adaptive oversampling: compute target pack size per domain using a function of production traffic, model sensitivity (measured by prior quantization experiments), and business-criticality. 4) Mix-in global background prompts sampled from other domains to preserve cross-domain token coverage. 5) Produce both a "compact" pack (~1k prompts) for fast iterations and a "robust" pack (~10k prompts) for final calibration runs. 6) Store metadata (selection seed, clustering parameters, selection scores) to ensure reproducibility.
acceptance_criteria: Per-domain compact calibration packs generated for top 20 product domains with reproducible selection metadata
INT8 and FP8 calibration using the compact packs cause no more than 1.5% relative degradation on domain-level key metrics compared to FP16 baseline for 90% of domains
Anchor exemplars detect at least 95% of regressions that later manifest in larger robust pack runs
Automation pipeline can rebuild packs from raw production logs and embeddings within 8 hours
Documentation and a Confluence runbook for pack regeneration and for handling new domains
tasks: Instrument production logging to emit domain tag and prompt hash (ENG-23950)
Implement exemplar scoring service: traffic-weight + embedding-cluster-coverage + regression-score
Build anchor selection module and immutable anchor store
Implement adaptive oversampling formula and pack assembler
Add reproducibility metadata and seed management
Integrate pack generation into calibration CI (runtime-1.24) and schedule nightly regeneration
Run end-to-end quantization experiments for FP8 and INT8 on 20 domains
Publish results dashboard and release notes
experiment_plan: Datasets: production prompt trace (30 days), tokenized prompts, per-prompt embeddings; reserve 10% for holdout validation
Variations: compact pack vs robust pack; uniform vs adaptive oversample; with vs without anchor set
Metrics: domain-level accuracy (F1/EM/ROUGE depending on domain), response fluency score (PPL delta), hallucination rate (binary), latency and token throughput
Thresholds: aim for <=1.5% relative metric drop on domain accuracy for quantized models versus FP16 baseline; PPL delta < 10%
A/B: deploy quantized models behind feature flag to 1% of traffic for live validation after offline pass

notes: Trade-off: heavier oversampling increases calibration cost but reduces miss rate for low-volume domains.
Decision: keep compact vs robust packs to reduce iteration time during model tuning.
Future: consider learning-to-sample model that predicts exemplar utility for calibration based on small-run quantization fingerprints.
